subject: Film & Cinema
title: Dramatic Irony: When the Audience Knows More
description: One-minute skill: Dramatic Irony: When the Audience Knows More.

hook.text: The audience knows the shark is under the boat. The swimmers don't. That's dramatic irony.

buildup.text: Giving audiences information characters lack creates suspense, dread, or dark humor.

discovery.text: Hitchcock's bomb-under-the-table example is the purest illustration of this technique.

twist.text: Dramatic irony can also create comedy — audiences laugh because they see the mistake coming.

climax.text: The audience becomes complicit, unable to look away because they know what's coming.

punchline.text: Knowing more makes you feel more.

quiz.question: What is dramatic irony?
options: When the audience knows something the characters don't
